subject: Term-shift accelerator: usage snapshot, capacity ask, and proposed renewal terms
content:
From: Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Elliot Shaw <elliot.shaw@helioslabs.com>
Cc: Alex Porter <alex.porter@helioslabs.com>, Procurement <procurement@helioslabs.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Term-shift accelerator: usage snapshot, capacity ask, and proposed renewal terms

Hi Elliot / Alex —

Quick note to share a short snapshot of usage ahead of your renewal conversation next week and a pragmatic term-shift proposal that could get Helios the headroom you asked for while keeping unit economics stable. Attaching a CSV with daily token spend and a concise ROI note.

Key highlights (last 90 days):
- Average daily token consumption: 4.6M tokens/day (30-day moving avg 5.1M).
- Peak single-day: 9.8M (early May product experiment).
- Inference latency at your current Dedicated profile: P50 210ms / P95 420ms.
- Cost per 1M tokens (current): $14.2 — projected to $11.8 with a 20% commit uplift and modest quantization on non-critical endpoints.

Proposed short-term accelerator (90-day pilot):
1) Increase committed capacity by 30% (adds burst headroom + reserved slots for nightly batches).
2) Shorten billing cadence to monthly for the pilot (eases cash flow impacts).
3) Redwood to provide a one-time $25k credits for migration of two heavy batch pipelines to our prefix caching config.

Why this path? It smooths peaks, improves tail latency, and demonstrates the unit-cost delta with a small financial commitment — useful input for your procurement team if you want a larger multi-quarter commit later.

Can you confirm if procurement needs a bundled SLA amendment or if we should send the standard addendum and pilot SOW?

Thanks,
Grace
Grace Oconnor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0127

Attachments: 20280607-helios-usage-snapshot.csv (csv), 20280607-roi-note-Helios.pdf (pdf), 20280607-term-shift-proposal.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Elliot Shaw <elliot.shaw@helioslabs.com>
To: Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Porter <alex.porter@helioslabs.com>, Procurement <procurement@helioslabs.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Jun 2028 11:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Term-shift accelerator: usage snapshot, capacity ask, and proposed renewal terms

Thanks Grace — this is helpful. A few quick notes from our side:
- The May experiment drove most of the spike; we expect another similar event in Q3 as we ramp a beta cohort, so headroom is valuable.
- Procurement will need a short SOW that calls out the pilot objectives and rollback path. They prefer monthly cadence for pilots.
- Can Redwood guarantee the reserved slots won't be preempted during our ETL window (02:00–05:00 PT)? That's our main reliability ask.

I'll loop in Procurement formally if you can share SOW language and the SLA tweak.

—Elliot
Elliot Shaw
Head of Product, Helios Labs
elliot.shaw@helioslabs.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 7 Jun 2028 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Term-shift accelerator: usage snapshot, capacity ask, and proposed renewal terms

Grace — good framing. I ran numbers off the CSV: 30% commit uplift reduces blended per-token cost by ~17% (matches your projection). Couple of tactical asks before we send SOW:
1) Confirm which endpoints benefit from prefix caching vs which need fp16 (we should avoid quantizing the 1:1 chat endpoint).
2) Confirm estimated monthly overage exposure if Helios hits a 2x peak (safety for procurement).

I can draft a price ladder for the pilot and the follow-on 12-month commit if you want — will make procurement happy.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Looping in Soojin for ops and SLA confirmation. Soojin — quick context:
- Customer wants reserved slots for nightly batch window 02:00–05:00 PT.
- Pilot is 90 days, monthly billing, 30% commit uplift.
- We commit to a one-time $25k credit tied to migrating two batch pipelines to caching.

Soojin — can you confirm whether Dedicated pool isolation and reservation can guarantee their ETL window non-preemption? If not, what mitigations (e.g., scheduled jobs, quota reservations) do we propose? Also, operational runbook needs to include an on-call contact and an escalation SLA during the pilot.

Thanks —
Marissa

Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 8 Jun 2028 11:31:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Term-shift accelerator: usage snapshot, capacity ask, and proposed renewal terms

Marissa / team — ops ok on this with a couple of guardrails:
- We can carve out reserved slots for their ETL window by pinning 12 dedicated instances in the pool during 02:00–05:00 PT. That will be flagged as reserved for Helios for the pilot.
- We'll add a scheduled autoscale policy outside that window to allow utilization for burst customers; reservations are strictly honored during the pinned window.
- I will prepare a short runbook and an on-call rotation entry for the pilot (will include escalation paths and playbooks for cold-start slowdowns).

I'll attach the draft runbook and a short SLA snippet to the SOW.

Soojin
Soojin Lee
Head of Customer Operations, Redwood Inference

Elliot / Alex / Procurement —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Per the thread above we propose the following next steps so procurement has what they need: 
1) SOW + Pilot Addendum (includes objectives, rollback path, monthly billing cadence) — attached: 20280607-term-shift-proposal.xlsx
2) Runbook + SLA snippet (reserved pin during 02:00–05:00 PT, escalation contact) — attached: 20280608-pilot-runbook-draft.md
3) Price ladder (pilot pricing + 12-month commit options) — Ben will send a short price ladder this afternoon.
4) Signature and kick-off target: earliest possible start 2028-07-02 if procurement signs by 2028-06-24.

Action items for Helios: confirm whether procurement wants the 90-day pilot as a standalone or bundled into a larger 12-month commitment (we can provide credit offsets either way). Also confirm any internal compliance docs they need attached to the SOW.

If procurement confirms cadence and required paperwork, Ben and I will finalize the pricing ladder and send an updated SOW with signatures ready.

Best,
Grace
